home.title: DeepSeek Harness plugin interface guide
home.lede: Choose whether a feature belongs in global settings, navigation, the current conversation or an auxiliary view; then use a documented DSH seat and actual controls. Screenshots stay local for review.
home.sectionHint: Choose the host area before patterns or controls
home.indexHint: Look up public seats, product-visible controls, icons and tokens
home.runtime: Clean screenshots use an isolated DSH web profile with official DeepSeek bundles only. Third-party plugins and user sessions are not copied; desktop-only account UI is described separately.
home.verify: The site renders structural HTML examples and keeps screenshots in docs/reference for local review. npm run site regenerates the data; npm run verify checks routes and browser rendering.

why.title: Background and goals
why.lede: This is not a brand style manual. It explains the regions and public extension seats in DeepSeek Harness, starting with the relationship between global preferences, settings pages, the sidebar, the conversation and the host rightbar.
why.missingTitle: Placement decisions plugin authors need to make

items.tokens: A ready-made set of values for colour, type, radius, spacing and elevation, in light and dark.
items.primitives: Buttons, switches, inputs, menus and notices already ship with the product, along with one explicit instruction: do not copy a control that already exists.
items.seats: A list of everywhere UI can go: what each spot is for, how many plugins fit, and whether it covers official UI.
items.icons: An icon set with a consistent naming scheme and size families, so a redrawn glyph does not drift.
items.aesthetics: Choose placement by content scope and relationship to the host. Discuss colour and dimensions only when product source or clearly labelled community guidance supports them.
items.force: This is a community reference, not a runtime enforcement mechanism; document compatibility exceptions.
items.invent: It does not invent values. Cite the source of each size, gap and duration; label recommendations where no official value exists.

gaps.layoutClaim: Multiple extensions can compete for the same sidebar space.
gaps.layoutBody: Official extension points identify purpose and type, but plugin page width, information density and relationship to the conversation still depend on the use case. Without a shared reference, content may overlap or leave unused space.
gaps.orderClaim: The display order of extensions in one seat may depend on load order.
gaps.orderBody: List seats sort by order; omitted or duplicate values make the result hard to explain. A community guide can help authors justify ordering, but a local plugin snapshot is not a universal deployment fact.
gaps.motionClaim: Similar interface actions can use inconsistent motion timing.
gaps.motionBody: Implementations may differ in duration, easing and reduced-motion behavior. Separate existing official control behavior from recommendations for new plugin UI, and avoid unsupported overrides.
gaps.iconGeometryClaim: Custom icons can differ from official icons in visual weight or alignment.
gaps.iconGeometryBody: Canvas size, path inset, stroke and baseline all affect how icons read together. Reuse existing icons and compare real geometry instead of redrawing by eye.
gaps.conflictClaim: Extensions that use the same seat may overlap or appear in an unclear order.
gaps.conflictBody: An extension API does not guarantee that contributions can all be shown together. Check the seat type, occupancy snapshot and alternatives, and state when the evidence was collected.

proof.overlay: shell.overlay is a host layer for frame-wide floating UI. The dsh-widgets rail registers in conversation.input.overlay; the two seats have different scopes and stacking.
proof.settings: settings.general.item adds one preference row; settings.section adds a page inside the host Settings window. The public seat list has no dedicated plugin-window seat.

why.asideNote: Clean screenshots are stored in docs/reference/clean-capture for local review. The website does not embed them. A blank profile does not render session view tabs because those appear after a conversation starts.
why.closing: Choose placement before styling. When a layout belongs to a plugin, identify its source and seat; do not describe one plugin installation as the default DSH interface.

spec.title: Design spec
spec.lede: In reading order. If you are writing your first plugin, start with the page skeleton and seat selection.
spec.relatedNote: The checkable clauses in the spec map to the checklist and the auditor's rules.

components.title: Interface elements
components.lede: Browse DSH-visible controls and layouts by interface task. HTML pages are structural examples; product screenshots remain in local review files and are never embedded. States without reliable runtime or source evidence are withheld.
components.demoLabel: HTML structure example, not a product screenshot
components.withheldText: No clean capture verifies this state; the HTML example stays hidden.
components.docSpecNote: This one is for engineers and agents: where the numbers came from, the API, the tokens, and the constraints a machine can check.
components.usage: The site renders HTML structure examples only. Screenshots stay in docs/reference/clean-capture for one-by-one review; plugin content is labelled separately from host UI.
components.screenshotCheckedNote: Product screenshots are used for local review only and are not embedded in the site.
components.sourceVerifiedNote: This structure is cross-checked against official source and the user-provided reference; no conversation text is invented.

seats.title: Seat directory
seats.lede: Use the content scope and task relationship to find a public place for a plugin interface.
seats.riskyNote: {n} of them cover official UI once you occupy them. Use those only when you really mean to replace that part of the interface.

kinds.single: single — one occupant only; a later registration covers an earlier one
kinds.list: list — as many as you like, sorted by order from low to high
kinds.keyed: keyed — handed out by key, one slot each
kinds.chain: chain — a selector decides; the whole chain can be replaced

scopes.root: root — global, present even with no session
scopes.maybe: session-maybe — tied to a session, but can be empty
scopes.session: session — appears once a session is selected

seats.orderNote: Start with the list spot whose meaning fits best; if none does, fall back to a single spot; leave the ones that cover official UI for last.

icons.title: Official icon set
icons.lede: {n} icons, lifted from the product exactly as they are, shapes untouched. Naming: ic_ds_<name>_<style>_<size>. Click one to copy its SVG.
icons.familyTail: If you draw your own, match the stroke weight and the breathing room of the icons beside it.
icons.why: Reusing official icons preserves the product vocabulary and avoids redrawing a shape that already has a source.

tokens.title: Design tokens
tokens.lede: {palette} colour values back {aliases} named colours. Use the names, not the values — light and dark are already worked out.
tokens.usageNote: Reach for a token name, never a hard-coded value. The first thing to give way in dark mode is a colour written into the stylesheet.
tokens.depth: Express depth with background layers (bg-base → bg-layer-1 → bg-layer-2 → bg-overlay), not with shadows. A shadow is the exception, not the default.
tokens.source: Values come straight from the theme definition inside the product's client bundle, one set per theme, unmodified.
tokens.geometryLead: The other half of the system. There are six corner steps and three elevation recipes — put two surfaces side by side and one step off shows. A surface that sits in the flow gets a 0.5px hairline; only what floats gets elevation, and the two never stack on one element.

geometryUse.--dsw-radius-xl: Cards: the card on a settings page (this repository's Card uses this step)
geometryUse.--dsw-radius-panel: Large: the composer card, a full-screen panel
geometryUse.--dsw-elevation-stroke: The 0.5px stroke every elevation recipe starts from
geometryUse.--dsw-elevation-panel: Floating controls: small buttons above content
geometryUse.--dsw-elevation-soft: Large floating surfaces: wider and softer

tokens.geometryNote: These values are read out of the product's theme layer the same way the colours are (the scale group in data/tokens.json); one set serves both themes.

inventory.title: Element inventory
inventory.lede: Scanning the running interface turns up {identities} identities: {official} belong to the product itself (the table below) and {third} come from third-party plugins (parked at the end). Of the product's own, {described} have their measured size written into the spec, while {notDescribed} are only placed — the file they belong to is known, but it does not state their size yet.
inventory.empty: Not scanned yet. Run node scripts/scan-ui.mjs on this machine: it opens the product, walks every state, and registers each element it can see.
inventory.note: "Covered" only means some file in this repository happened to contain the word; it is not a review. "Gap" is the to-do list — and each of those still needs a human call: it may be something the product really has and the spec missed, or it may just be a one-off container. Third-party elements are all parked: they are not DSH's interface language, and the product's own side comes first.
inventory.tableTitle: {n} identities that belong to the product
inventory.thirdHint: Grouped by plugin, counted not expanded
inventory.thirdNote: These screens are drawn by installed plugins: sliders, heatmaps, stat cards, their own switches. The product itself has none of it. They are registered here (who drew it, how big, where it shows up) and left alone until the product's own elements are done — only then is it worth deciding whether plugin authors should get a recommendation.
inventory.how: scripts/scan-ui.mjs drives the product with the same credentials the screenshot script uses, walks it state by state, and registers every element that occupies space under an identity with the CSS Modules hash stripped off: tag, role, box, computed styles, seat, and the screens it showed up on. It is machine output, so its unit is "things you can see", not "components".
inventory.stateNote: Documented: the file the anchor points at really contains this element's measured size (a `50 × 50` style pair, units optional). Placed only: it knows which file it belongs to, but that file does not state its size yet — this is the main to-do. Referenced: some text merely happened to contain the word; needs review. Plugin-only: an installed plugin draws it (anything under dsx-, for instance), so the product itself has no such element. Gap: neither side mentions it.
